messages:
oliver: FYI hitting a confusing TypeError when calling the sync helper on the Python SDK: "'coroutine' object is not awaitable". looks like our sync wrapper is returning a coroutine in some code paths.

sana: can you paste the snippet you used? are you calling `client.generate_sync(...)` or `client.generate(...).result()`?

oliver: minimal repro:
```py
from redwood import Client
c = Client()  # sync client
resp = c.generate_sync('hello')  # supposed to be blocking
print(resp)
```
stack: TypeError: 'coroutine' object is not awaitable

leo: ah interesting. generate_sync delegates to the async path and we try to detect loop vs no-loop, but in the branch where httpx pool is lazy-created we return the coroutine instead of awaiting it. my bad.

rachel: this also makes typing misleading: the stub says -> GenerationResponse but sometimes it returns Coroutine[Any,...]. Users (and mypy) get confused.

oliver: I ran into this in a Flask app during startup where we create a Client globally. some handlers call `generate_sync` and it fails intermittently depending on worker model.

sana: three parts to fix: 1) runtime safety (never leak coroutine to sync callers), 2) clear error message if user accidentally calls async method from sync context, 3) typing fixes (overloads / explicit sync API surface).

leo: for (1) quick patch: in the sync wrapper do `res = asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(self._generate_async(...))` when there's no running loop. But be careful under uvicorn/gunicorn where loop already running -> raise a helpful error recommending `await` or use `anyio`/threadpool.

rachel: prefer approach: implement a true sync code path using httpx.Client for sync methods. this avoids messing with event loop and is better for WSGI apps. we already have an httpx sync transport available in the runtime; just add a small adapter that mirrors the async method behavior.

oliver: that sounds ideal long-term. short-term can add an explicit runtime check: if inspect.iscoroutine(result): raise RuntimeError("Sync method returned coroutine. This indicates an internal bug; please upgrade to >=x.y.z or use async client.") with link to issue. That will make failures clear instead of opaque TypeError.

sana: for typings: add overloads in stubs: `def generate_sync(...) -> GenerationResponse` and `async def generate(...) -> GenerationResponse`. also add py.typed marker and update mypy config in repo to catch mismatches.

leo: I'll open a PR to implement the sync httpx client adapter + unit tests that assert no coroutine is returned. include two integration tests: WSGI-style process (requests in threadpool) and ASGI (async).

dev-bot: CI started for branch fix/sync-adapter-typing (build 981)

rachel: small doc note: update the quickstart to recommend creating clients inside app factories rather than module import time, and show both sync and async examples. also add FAQ: "Why am I seeing 'coroutine' object not awaitable?" with explanation.

oliver: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/702 for follow-up to improve type stubs and consider exporting separate `SyncClient` class. linking to the PR when ready.

leo: PR WIP: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/389 — includes fix and tests. I'll tag people for review.

oliver: thanks all. landed workaround in our app for now but will switch to the new release once it's out. closing thread when PR merges. :shipit:
